title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
notes:
Task: Given a BST and two existing nodes p and q, return their lowest common ancestor.
Idea: Walk left when both values are smaller, right when both are larger; otherwise the current node is the split point.
Invariant: The maintained traversal, window, partition, or prefix state remains sufficient to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty/small permitted inputs, duplicate values, and boundary cases are handled where the problem constraints allow.
complexity_reason: Walk left when both values are smaller, right when both are larger; otherwise the current node is the split point.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
notes:
Task: Find the duplicate in an array of n+1 values in [1,n] without modifying the array.
Idea: Count values at most mid; a count greater than mid means the duplicate lies in the lower half.
Invariant: The maintained traversal, window, partition, or prefix state remains sufficient to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty/small permitted inputs, duplicate values, and boundary cases are handled where the problem constraints allow.
complexity_reason: Count values at most mid; a count greater than mid means the duplicate lies in the lower half.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
notes:
Task: Design addNum and findMedian for a stream of integers.
Idea: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and min-heap for the upper half, balanced so lower has at most one extra item.
Invariant: The maintained traversal, window, partition, or prefix state remains sufficient to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty/small permitted inputs, duplicate values, and boundary cases are handled where the problem constraints allow.
time_complexity: O(log n) per insertion; O(1) median
complexity_reason: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and min-heap for the upper half, balanced so lower has at most one extra item.
